_comment: Placeholder recipes carried over from the MINCECRAFT simulator. Percentages are of the captured base weight. Edit here; the panel reloads them on refresh.
_scales_note: Two scales. An ingredient goes on whichever one can actually hold the recipe's percentage tolerance. The main scale can only manage 'percent' once 2 divisions fit inside it, i.e. above 2*division/percent grams; below that the small scale takes over, up to its usable capacity (capacity minus the tare of whatever container sits on it). Set 'connected': true for the small scale only if it is wired to the Pi and streams the same frame format — otherwise the operator reads its display and keys the value in, and the main scale corroborates.

small.name: Bench scale
small._note: SPEC NOT CONFIRMED — defaults assume a 3 kg x 0.1 g bench scale. Check the label and correct division_g, capacity_g and usable_g before this goes on the floor.

scales._crossover_note: null = derive it (2*main.division_g / tolerance.percent = 500 g here). Set a number to override: lower means more ingredients stay on the floor scale, which is easier to pour into but holds a looser tolerance — recipe review shows exactly which ingredients are affected and by how much.

_tolerance_note: floor_g is a backstop only. With two scales the crossover does the real work: nothing reaches the main scale that the main scale cannot hold to 'percent'.

water._note: Water depends on the day's flour, so it is not a recipe percentage. A supervisor sets water/flour each production day; the station will not start a batch until they have. A recipe is gated only if it names both a flour_ingredient and a water_ingredient.
water._day_start_note: 0 = plain calendar day. Set to e.g. 6 if a night shift runs past midnight, so the lock lands between shifts instead of mid-shift.

_products_note: meat: which animal this product is made from, so the operator is not asked. null means not decided yet — the batch records it as unspecified. draft: true means the recipe has no ingredients yet; the panel shows it but will not start a batch on it. Fill them in DOKI-Recipes.xlsx and run xlsx_to_recipes.py. Teriyaki omits liquid smoke, which the source CSV lists with a quantity of zero.
